title: We are making an AI-Chat Game "Cursed Realm"
author: fallhunter
selftext: Our team is making a chat game driven by AI, in which the core gameplay is chatting with NPC to get clues and stuff.  join the closed beta here: [https://cr.capplay.io](https://cr.capplay.io/#/)

comments.author: lalalandcity1
comments.body:
What app did you use to create the graphics?

Also is Unity the engine?

replies.author: fallhunter
replies.body: No, we just use web technologies. For images we use some Ai tools.

replies.author: lalalandcity1
replies.body: Which AI tools? Which web technologies? This is an aigamedev forum.

replies.author: fallhunter
replies.body: I don’t think a game must be made by Unity or typical game engine. Lol.

replies.author: lalalandcity1
replies.body: What web technologies did you use? What AI tools did you use for the image generation? Why are answering these questions so difficult?

replies.author: FjorgVanDerPlorg
replies.body:
What the other user means is why are you treating your fellow gamedevs like customers? This is a gamedev sub where we discuss our work/workflows, you seem to have it confused it with subs like /r/indiegames, where you can market towards people interested in playing games, not making them.

PS They are actually asking about your workflow because they are curious how you're doing it.

replies.author: fallhunter
replies.body: Thanks for the explanation! I see. Glad to share our work flow: chatgpt + midjourney + VUE.js + typescript + firebase.  Btw I am not trying to market customers, the game is still under development. Want to know what do you think from a developer/designer perspective:)

replies.author: FjorgVanDerPlorg
replies.body:
Yeah so many devs make the mistake of marketing in gamedev spaces, in cases like yours you basically have to fight that assumption when you ask for feedback from fellow developers. Like go out of your way to make it clear you want opinions and be specific on what aspects, eg part of the UI or a specific gameplay element.

I also always ask for "constructive criticism", people on average seem more willing to focus on what you are doing wrong, than what they think is right, often because problems tend to stand out more to a practiced eye.

Also in the case of web apps, trust is an issue that will hurt uptake. Gamedevs get targeted by scammers a lot, so going to a unknown site and trusting it to run code on our machines can be a big ask. You can easily get around this by posting screenshots or video of the UI/gameplay etc.

It sucks that all this is even necessary, but unfortunately it gets added to the list of nice things we can't have because of scammers and other bad actors...
